Present : Mr. Rajiv Atma Ram, Sr. Advocate
 with Mr. Arjun Pratap Atma Ram, Advocate
 for the petitioner.

***
1. Whether Reporters of local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
2. To be referred to the Reporters or not?
3. Whether the judgment should be reported in the Digest?

The grievance raised in this petition is that members of the petitioner-Food Safety Officer's Association were working as Food Inspectors under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which has now been substituted as Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') and they have now re-designated as Food Safety Inspectors under the new Act.

As per the learned senior counsel they are fully eligible to be appointed as Designated Officers and, in fact some of the members of the petitioner-Association have been nominated by the State and imparted training.
Further as per the learned senior counsel an employee can be appointed as whole time Designated Officer under the Act.
The post of Designated Officer is a whole time job but now the Food Safety Officer'S Association vs Union Of India And Others on 18 April, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181439402/

entities.text: Food Safety Officer'S Association vs Union Of India And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Government has appointed such officers as Designated Officers who by virtue of the office they hold can only work on the post of Designated Officer on part time basis in addition to the other multi-farious charges being given to them.

Learned senior counsel states that in this regard the petitioner- Association has also moved a representation (Annexure P-10) and that at this stage he would be satisfied if the said representation is decided by respondent No.3 by passing a speaking order within any reasonable time.
I find this to be a fair request.

In the circumstances, without going into the merits of the case, this petition is disposed of with a direction to respondent No.3 to decide the representation (Annexure P-10) by passing a speaking order thereon within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
A copy of this order be given dasti to learned counsel for the petitioner on payment of usual charges.
